In twenty twenty-two, a war threatened the machines that make your chips!
How can a war stop chip factories?
Chipmaking lasers run on neon gas. And about half the world's chip-grade neon came from Ukraine.
From just two companies, in Odesa and Mariupol.
Exactly. When Russia invaded, both plants stopped.
So why didn't the world run out of chips?
Because of an earlier war. When Russia seized Crimea in twenty fourteen, neon prices jumped six hundred percent.
Chipmakers learned. They found new suppliers in China and Korea, and began recycling their neon.
In twenty twenty-two, one supplier said prices rose up to five hundred percent... but no chip factory stopped.
